title: Landing Gear — Nose Wheel Steering — Conversion to the Standard 3 Machined Manifold
abstract: Conversion of in-service aircraft to the standard 3 machined steering manifold, which integrates filtration, accumulator charging and the position pick-off in one block and removes four external fittings from the nose gear bay.

sections.planning_reason: The interim filter kit cut the steering jitter reporting rate by four fifths but left a 4000 flight hour filter change that operators consistently describe as intrusive, and the residual events still cluster in the first hundred hours after a green system component change. The built-up manifold is also the largest single source of hydraulic leakage in the nose gear bay, at nineteen reported leaks per million flight hours, nearly all at the accumulator charging port. Aircraft that are not converted keep both the short filter interval and the leakage exposure.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin replaces the built-up steering manifold with a machined block in which the filter cavity, the accumulator charging gallery and the position sensor pick-off are integrated. The accumulator is retained and is charged through a face port, which removes the external hose and four fittings. The filter remains a service item but sits in a cavity sized for a 5000 flight hour interval.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on its wheels with the nose gear down and locked and install the ground locks. Depressurise the green hydraulic system and discharge the accumulator. Get access through the nose gear bay in zones 711 and 714 and open the nose gear doors in zone 741. Disconnect and cap the manifold pipework. Remove the built-up manifold following task AMM-Z-32-20-12-000-025-A. Install the machined block D3220127361550 on the existing hard points. Transfer the accumulator D3220121572714 to the face port and install the new seal. Install the filter D3220123507496 in the block cavity. Re-connect the pipework to the revised end fittings and torque to the values in the instructions. Install the position sensor at FIN 9WS, the non-return valve at FIN 2820WS5 and the accumulator sensing line at FIN 25GB on the new block face. Install the manifold following task AMM-Z-32-20-12-400-025-A. Pressurise the green system, check for leaks and re-charge the accumulator. Do the steering rig check and the full travel operational test.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to ZEPHYR-20, ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 aircraft already carrying the interim filter and seal kit and not delivered at the standard 3 configuration. Aircraft that never had the interim kit must have it assessed before conversion, because the servo may still hold debris.
sections.material_note: Kit K3220-1258-01 contains the machined block, the accumulator face seal, the filter, the revised pipework end fittings and the sensor hardware for one aircraft. The machined block is a long-lead item at twenty-six weeks. The removed manifold is returned to Aeralis for credit.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's convenience during a base maintenance visit. Operators wishing to delete the 4000 flight hour filter change should embody within 36 months.
